Walter Russell Mead (@wrmead) on why tech companies are starting to demand their employees be patriotic:

"Increasingly, companies are starting to realize that they need their employees to be patriotic. 

That is, your employees need to think it's an evil sin to sell IP to China. 

And that your coworkers will rat you out in a heartbeat if they think you're doing something like that.

One of the biggest things that happened in modern American history is the mutual discovery of tech and government. 

In the 1990s, companies would say, I'm not an American company, I'm a global company, and nowhere was that stronger than in the world of tech, where Google has no boundaries.

Today, tech is actually the locus of international great power competition. 

China's attempt to build a technosphere that can dominate the American technosphere is critical to your business, but also to the American state, to power and independence. 

So much to the surprise of both the tech world and the political world, they've been driven in on each other, and there's a kind of re-nationalization of tech.

If you're a legacy multinational, free trade is the essence of your business. I need financial markets, labor markets, and manufactured good markets that are seamless and open. 

But if you're a tech company, you don't. Google is not importing and exporting a lot of goods. 

You're much more concerned about security of supply chain, security of intellectual property."

If AI finds a vulnerability in Bitcoin node software or attacks a mining pool, developers can release a patch and node operators/mining pools can update. That doesn't require everyone in Bitcoin to agree on some huge change to the network.

But markets don't wait for patches.

With quantum computing also becoming a longer-term concern, the industry needs to get ahead of these risks instead of reacting after something breaks.

Onchain the most exciting I've seen it for quite a long time.

- Crypto demands better tokenomics now and tokens that are aligned with token holders, so we are seeing much better tokens for holders with buybacks and burns. Even newer launches are adding to the buy pressure if they are successful e.g. STONK. 

Long live crypto.

Instead of looking at the pool APR and jumping in, you can open the actual LP positions and see their range, age, PnL, ROI, fee APR and liquidity.

Find a stock pool getting real volume
 → Check existing LPs on Revert
 → Compare different fee tiers/ranges
 → Look at how long the position has actually been earning
 → Then decide if the fees are worth the LP risk

Everyone is staring at the token doing 10x and overlooking who's collecting fees from all of them.

LPing can be worth it if @RobinhoodCrypto Chain keeps going this direction.

i've been grinding hard for over a year now. if you are over 35 years old and have 30+ pounds to lose, here's my advice:

- the first step is understanding that something in your lifestyle is very broken. probably not just one thing, either
- you didn't gain all of that weight in a few months, nor will you lose it in a few months. to make it truly sustainable and fueled by permanent lifestyle changes, adjust your time horizon to 1-2 years
- focus on improving your fitness first rather than losing weight, with a foundation of progressive overload resistance training (lifting  heavy weights to within ~3 reps of failure) at least 2x per week some other activity you enjoy 2x per week (for me it's yoga). make sure you walk long distances on off days, and on every other day that you reasonably can
- spend ~3-4 months building up muscle (especially if you are de-conditioned) before making big changes to your diet
- cook your own meals for 80% to 90% of what you eat. meal prep absolutely works if you don't eat junk snacks in-between meals (look for recipes on YouTube). use AI to create healthy, batch recipes of your favorite foods if needed. cook batches of 6-8 servings and freeze them in high quality containers designed for this purpose. plan out what you will eat in advance the next day
- prioritize protein intake (up to 1 gram per pound of target bodyweight, though i personally do closer to 0.75-0.8 g). don't regularly eat junk carbs (like chips, candy, and cakes). eat only when you are hungry, but try to get 3 meals per day to keep your protein intake consistent
- when you start to lose fat, your appearance might not change much due to muscle backfilling it. you may go ~6 months without noticing any big visual changes. monitor body fat mass vs lean muscle mass using either dexa scan or a well-calibrated impedance sensor scale for directional data
